faq.a: Heart valves are one-way doors. They open to let blood move forward and snap shut to stop it flowing backwards, so each heartbeat pushes blood in one direction only.
asks: What is a heart valve for?
Why does the heart need valves?

faq.q: What is the difference between the tricuspid and mitral valves?
faq.a: Both sit between a top chamber and a bottom chamber. The tricuspid valve is on the right side and has three flaps; the mitral valve is on the left side and has two flaps.
asks: Tell me about the tricuspid valve
Tell me about the mitral valve

faq.q: What does the aortic valve do?
faq.a: The aortic valve is the exit door from the left ventricle into the aorta, the biggest artery. It opens when the ventricle squeezes and shuts when it relaxes, so blood sent to the body cannot fall back into the heart.
asks: Tell me about the aortic valve
Which valve lets blood out to the body?

faq.q: How many valves does the heart have?
faq.a: Four: the tricuspid and pulmonary valves on the right side, and the mitral and aortic valves on the left side.

faq.q: What opens and closes the valves?
faq.a: Blood pressure does. Valves have no muscles of their own; when pressure behind a flap is higher than in front, it swings open, and when the pressure reverses it is pushed shut.
asks: How does a valve know when to shut?

facts: The human heart has four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral and aortic.
The mitral valve has two flaps, or cusps; the tricuspid valve has three.
Heart valves are opened and closed by differences in blood pressure, not by muscles of their own.

quiz.why: Valves are passive flaps. When blood tries to flow backwards it pushes the flaps together and seals them.

wrong.0: Valve flaps have no muscles that close them; the strings attached only stop them flipping over.
wrong.2: The brain does not open or close valves; pressure changes do it every beat.
